teaching.task: Predict fixed-temperature gas compression/expansion and distinguish an inert-gas pressure rise at fixed volume from compression.
teaching.causalExplanation: Compression initially puts unchanged gas amounts into less space, increasing wall impact frequency and pressure. Net reaction toward fewer gaseous moles partly offsets that increase. Inert gas at fixed volume/T changes total pressure without changing reacting partial pressures. Coefficients represent stoichiometry, not an elementary rate law.
